newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli banks shut down by strike.
newsitem.headline: Israeli banks shut down by strike.

text.p: Israeli bank workers shut down the country's banks on Friday in violation of a court order ruling workers could strike for only half the day, a senior banker said.
It was the third consecutive Friday workers went on strike, demanding a five-day work week. Banks at border crossings and direct banking services remained open, as well as some of the smaller banks.
"There was a feeling that we could have reached an agreement and that this week the court order would be upheld," Bank Association Director Freddy Vider told Israel radio.

Israel's attorney-general asked the High Court on Thursday to impose fines on union leaders for violating last week's labour court decision ordering workers to work at least half the banks' Friday hours.
"It will be very seroius not only if workers strike...but intend to continue to do things against the order," Vider said.
Union officials say management has been bargaining in bad faith, prompting bank workers to continue their sanctions.
Zion Shema, head of the Histadrut labour federation's bank workers union said on Thursday banks had agreed to move to a five-day work week but were refusing to implement the agreement.
Israeli banks operate Sunday through Thursday and for a half day on Friday.

Bank officials have said agreements to coordinate a move to a five-day week were rejected by Israel's anti-trust authorities, which ruled the banks could not make a collective decision to stop providing service on Friday.
